extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, media researchers, and designers/analysts of news homepages
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and metrics for evaluating how news outlets select and present stories (hard vs. soft), how selection affects audience behavior, and recommended newsroom reforms to improve public-information outcomes. Useful for coding content, auditing homepages, or designing editorial strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft-News Proportion / Soft-News Increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the proportion of stories categorized as soft news (lifestyle, celebrity, human interest, sensational crime) versus hard news; Patterson documents a large increase from ~25% in 1980 to ~50% by 2000 in some samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize by coding stories as 'soft' (examples: lifestyle, celebrity, human interest, sensational crime) or 'hard' (policy, process). Use time-series comparison to quantify 'drift' toward soft content; use as baseline for outlet placement on a hard–soft continuum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: Increased Critical / Negative Framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the degree to which coverage uses critical or negative framing of leaders and institutions; Patterson documents a shift toward more critical/negative tone and less positive coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code tone (positive/neutral/negative) across stories and beats. Note that excessive negativity can alienate audiences; balance is a metric for evaluating editorial decisions (especially during election coverage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which policy and public-affairs stories are framed around individual leaders' personalities and private lives rather than institutional actions and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify stories that center on individuals versus institutional explanations. Reduction in personalization is a recommended reform; measure placement and prominence of personalized stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of emphasis on sensational events — crime, scandal, disaster — relative to policy and process coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code story topics and framing for sensational elements (scandal, dramatic imagery, lurid detail). Patterson recommends reducing sensational/soft content, especially on evening news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter Voice / Embedded Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which reporters insert opinion, interpretation, or their own voice within ostensibly factual reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify use of reporter-as-interpreter language vs. source-based reporting. Patterson recommends 'slowing the reporter's voice' and returning to source-based reporting as a quality criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias toward selecting stories because they are photogenic or visually compelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure story selection for visual elements or ease of visual presentation; note that visualizability often drives placement and prominence on homepages and broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict / Controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias toward selecting and emphasizing stories that involve dispute, conflict, or controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code for presence of adversarial frames, dispute-centered headlines, or conflict-driven narratives; track how conflict-orientation affects audience engagement and democratic information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick Resolution Preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for stories with rapid story-arcs (quick resolution) rather than ongoing, complex situations requiring sustained coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether outlets favor episodic, easily-resolved items over long-term explanatory or follow-up reporting; measure persistence/follow-through on complex issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrity-Adjacency
rubrics_metrics.description: Favoring stories that have a celebrity hook or adjacency, increasing placement and prominence regardless of substantive public-interest value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify celebrity-linked story selection and prominence; contrast with substantive policy coverage to assess newsworthiness trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Stickiness Predictions (Editorial Heuristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions driven by predictions about what will keep audiences from switching channels / clicking away (i.e., presumed 'stickiness').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat editorial 'predicted stickiness' as an explicit, testable criterion: compare editorial predictions to measured audience behavior (time on page, retention, cross-platform consumption). Patterson argues these predictions often diverge from actual audience preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard-news Consumers Are Heavier News Users
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience metric: people who prefer hard news consume more news overall than those who prefer soft news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment audiences by stated preference or consumption patterns; measure total news exposure across segments to inform whether serving soft news attracts heavy consumers or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft News Fails to Retain or Grow Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical test: whether increasing soft-news content correlates with audience retention or growth; Patterson finds soft news has not retained the audience and audiences declined despite the shift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal audience metrics to test whether soft-content strategies meet their retention goals; treat failure to retain as evidence against the 'give the audience what it wants' justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience Preference Bimodality
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience distribution metric: the population is bimodal — a serious-news audience and a near-non-audience exist, with little middle ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze audience segmentation and polarization of engagement levels; tailor homepage strategies knowing a large low-engagement segment may not be won by soft-content tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Tone Alienates Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect metric: excessively negative or critical coverage tends to drive audiences away rather than increase engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the relationship between tone and audience metrics (viewership, clicks, trust). Use as a constraint when setting editorial tone, especially for election coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce Sensational / Soft Content (Editorial Reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended production standard: intentionally cut back on sensational and soft content, particularly on prime programs like evening news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply editorial policies to limit lifestyle/celebrity/crime-sensational stories in core news slots; monitor changes in audience knowledge and accountability indicators after implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce Critical / Negative Tone (Editorial Reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended production standard: moderate the use of critical or negative framing, especially during elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt tone guidelines that prioritize balanced, contextualized coverage; code election coverage for tone and provide training to avoid default negativity that may alienate audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide More Substantive Policy Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended production standard: increase the quantity and quality of substantive policy reporting rather than personality or sensational angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize explanatory reporting, policy context, and process coverage; measure placement and depth (e.g., policy detail, sources, explanatory background) on homepages and newscasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce Personalization of Policy and Process Stories (Editorial Reform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended production standard: avoid framing institutional or policy issues primarily through individual personalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce style/editorial rules to foreground institutions, processes, and systemic explanations; audit stories for personalization bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow the Reporter’s Voice / Return to Source-Based Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended production standard: limit reporter-as-interpreter insertions and emphasize sourcing and attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt standards favoring quoted sources, multiple perspectives, and avoidance of reporter-as-authoritative-interpretation; code stories for voice and sourcing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Documentation & Hard–Soft Continuum
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric/rubric: place outlets on a measurable hard–soft continuum using quantified content analysis (baseline for comparing outlets over time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic content coding to assign positions on the continuum; track movement over time as a performance metric for editorial strategy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizability via Coding Schemes (Reinemann et al. 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological guidance: the soft-news drift can be operationalized and tracked using existing three-dimensional coding schemes (e.g., Reinemann et al. 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt validated coding schemes to measure dimensions such as personalization, conflict orientation, and informational vs. entertaining content; document coding rules and inter-coder reliability for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for Audience–Supply-Side Mismatch (Homepage-Prediction Model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation criterion: assess whether producers' beliefs about audience desires diverge from measured audience consumption; Patterson suggests a homepage-prediction model can test this gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare editorial assumptions (surveys, heuristics) with observed consumption data (clicks, time-on-page, cross-platform usage) to validate or reject content strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic-Accountability Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Normative metric: how newsroom selection affects voters' policy knowledge and the capacity for electoral accountability; less hard news predicts weaker democratic accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure downstream civic outcomes (policy knowledge surveys, turnout correlations, informed voting indicators) to assess the public-interest performance of editorial choices.
